observedProcessWindows.limitation: Includes unsuccessful invocations with observed end times; excludes open intervals and gaps between invocations.

limits: Role intervals overlap; do not sum them as elapsed time.
Completed process unions exclude interrupted invocations; first-author acceptance spans retain interruption and resume gaps.
Input and authoring windows are subsets of each invocation.
Native execution supplies no output-stream/command-generation or pure reasoning durations.
Usage snapshots may be cumulative; no additive token or credit claim.
Byte counts cover recorded input payloads and returned text fields, not complete MCP transport bytes.
Latest acceptance can include renderer refresh or later reuse; first acceptance is reported separately.

findings.issue: Shore and Walk are rendered only as default text components. The lines say 'independently selectable', but the result contains no occurrence controls, selected state or focus showing which resulting objects are selected; its only control is Undo Ungroup. The assigned Ungroup interaction at /actions/6 requires showing the resulting objects and selection, and the review criteria require actual item selection where applicable. Concrete names and bounds alone do not demonstrate the promised independently selectable result.
findings.remedy: Represent Shore and Walk as distinct occurrence controls with a visible resulting selection and appropriate focus, or compose the exact accepted timeline dependency's Ungroup result through the supported child reference mechanism. Preserve the current inclusive boundaries, omitted source parts, unchanged neighboring clip and library definition, and Undo behavior.

findings.issue: The range-deleted result reduces the Music bed example to '00:20 End becomes 00:16 End'. The authored range-split example establishes that this bed spans both sides of the selected 04.000–07.967 interval. For that middle cut, /actions/0 and /feedback/0 explicitly require two unnamed video-owned outside occurrences. Neither resulting fragment is identified in range-deleted, so the scene does not demonstrate this consequential structure change and can be read as a simple shortening of one occurrence.
findings.remedy: Show the two retained outside portions as separate unnamed video-owned objects, with concrete inclusive boundaries and the later portion shifted left by the removed 120 frames. Keep the four-track scope, City lights shift, preserved outside content, edit location and one Undo operation consistent. This can be corrected within the existing result scene.

findings.issue: Both dismissed and range-dismissed leave the Selection actions trigger in the default state. The artifact's focusIntent promises focus restoration to that trigger, but neither capture visibly demonstrates it. The upstream dynamic return-target gap remains explicitly acknowledged.
findings.remedy: Show the representative dismissed-trigger in the supported focus state in both dismissal scenes while retaining the explicit limitation about the exact dynamic return target.

findings.issue: The single staged trim changes Coast montage from Start 04 / inclusive End 12 to Start 02 / inclusive End 15, then trim-applied commits both boundary changes and the City lights shift as one Undo operation. The assigned /actions/10 canonical interaction specifies trimming Start or End and explicitly keeps timeline End fixed during a Start trim. No intermediate interaction explains two separate boundary edits. The rendered example therefore demonstrates a different trim operation from the supplied source.
findings.remedy: Make the illustrated preview and applied result show one source-defined boundary edit. For example, retain Start 04 while extending End 12 to 15, reveal the hidden material at that edge, and show the required same-track collision shift as part of that one Undo operation. Keep group geometry, handles, summaries and outcome evidence consistent. If illustrating both boundary edits, make their separate interactions and Undo semantics explicit.

findings.issue: The source defines inclusive End boundaries, but the resulting clips are labeled Coast shore 04–08 and Coast walk 08–12, sharing frame 08 under that convention. In addition, excluded-note calls source intro 00–04 and outro 12–16 wholly excluded even though they meet the retained group's inclusive 04–12 interval at frames 04 and 12. No distinction between geometric cut positions and inclusive frame timestamps is supplied. Consequently the central visible-only Ungroup example does not establish nonoverlapping parts or correct preservation of the boundary frames required by /actions/27.
findings.remedy: Use consistent frame-aware representative boundaries. Distinguish geometric cut edges from inclusive frame endpoints if necessary, make adjacent included clips nonoverlapping, and place wholly excluded intro/outro parts strictly outside the retained interval. Update part-a, part-b, excluded-note, their geometry or labels as appropriate, and the associated outcome interpretation together. Preserve the included content and composed positions.

findings.issue: The open-menu scene renders both group-clip and ungroup-control in the focus state, giving two simultaneous focus outlines. This obscures the distinction between the retained object selection and the current keyboard target inside the menu. The ungroup-failure scene already distinguishes them correctly by keeping the group selected and focusing Retry Ungroup.
findings.remedy: Keep group-clip visibly selected while the menu is open, and reserve the focus state for ungroup-control. Update focusIntent to distinguish retained selection from menu focus.

findings.issue: Ungroup is rendered as a persistent primary button in the timeline action row beside the unopened Selection actions trigger. The same presentation persists in trim-preview, trim-applied and trim-invalid. The acceptance packet explicitly contextualizes this command: /flows/0/decisions/2 rejects a persistent Ungroup control in favor of Selection actions, and the ungroup-assembly action requires that menu to be open. No rendered state depicts that menu context. This is an inherited wireframe/source mismatch, not a new theme defect.
findings.remedy: Represent Ungroup within an explicitly opened Selection actions menu for one selected grouped occurrence, with its trigger and open context visually apparent. Keep it absent outside that menu state, and retain retry in the appropriate failed-operation context. Update the wireframe structure/state representation and obtain its acceptance before carrying the correction into UI; an existing assigned scene can depict the open menu.

findings.issue: The new open-menu scene depicts two simultaneous keyboard-focus targets: group-clip and ungroup-control both use state focus, and the screenshot visibly gives both the background grouped occurrence and the Ungroup item an outer focus ring. This conflates retained object selection with current menu focus. The ungroup-failure scene already distinguishes them correctly by setting the group to selected while Retry Ungroup has focus.
findings.remedy: In the group-menu-open UI scene, render group-clip in selected state with its selected variant retained, and keep focus on ungroup-control. Verify that the object remains visibly selected and only the active menu item has the keyboard-focus ring. Recheck the normal and failure menu scenes. This is a visual-state correction and does not require new behavior or structural changes.
